   Refactor validate() to guard clauses

   Context

   validate() in /tmp/collie-probe/validate.js uses three levels of nested if to reach a single return true. Flattening to guard clauses makes the failure conditions
   explicit up front and leaves the happy path at the bottom. Behavior is unchanged.

   Change

   validate.js — replace the nested body with early returns:

   function validate(user) {
     if (!user) return false;
     if (!user.email) return false;
     if (!user.email.includes("@")) return false;
     return true;
   }

   Export line stays as is.

   Verification

   node -e 'const {validate}=require("/tmp/collie-probe/validate.js"); console.log(validate(null), validate({}), validate({email:"a"}), validate({email:"a@b"}))'
   → expect false false false true.
